requirements.requirement: Repair bin/copy-image so the supplied 64 MiB sparse source is copied byte-for-byte with the same logical length while the destination uses less than 2 MiB of allocated space.
requirements.summary: The destination was 67,108,864 bytes, byte-identical to source.img by cmp and SHA-256, and allocated only 8,192 bytes. The same result was observed again after restart.
The source retained its prepared SHA-256, 67,108,864-byte length, 8 KiB allocation, permissions, ownership, and original timestamp through final verification.

requirements.requirement: Make repeated copying to an existing destination safe.
requirements.summary: The utility successfully replaced a dense pre-existing destination, repaired deliberate destination corruption on a second copy, and completed two consecutive post-restart copies with correct bytes and sparse allocation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution the node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The repaired POSIX-shell utility uses the already-installed coreutils cp implementation, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The repaired utility produces a byte-identical 64 MiB destination using only 8 KiB, preserves the source, safely handles repeated copies, retains the required OS and kernel, and remains functional after a fully evidenced node restart.
limitations: Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The baseline test file was created solely to establish behavior and removed in the same command (cmd-29991e779c694fed). The utility replacement and temporary rollback copy directly supported the repair, with the rollback file later removed (cmd-8a5f32b7c9f34772, cmd-ef7555bb8a3c4314). Dense allocation, deliberate destination corruption, and repeated overwrites were bounded tests against the chosen destination; usage-test files were removed (cmd-413bc16a21a5458c). The restart was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol, and subsequent destination writes verified recovery (cmd-3f0ed5e9a740492a, cmd-53fae39dbf54406c). Final evidence shows no temporary residue, failed units, new listeners, or package damage. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged restart, changed post-restart identity, and recovered system, SSH, data, and copy behavior; lifecycle boot identities independently agree.
